# karvi error codes

<!-- Generated by tools/errorcodegen from internal/errorcodes. Do not edit. -->

This table is generated from the error-code registry. Every distinct
cause has exactly one code, and codes are never reused. A code emitted by source
but missing here is a defect.

**Exit** is the process exit status when the code decides the result of a direct
activity (`login`, `command`, `config`, `daemon`, or a job rejected before
dispatch). Inside `run`, per-device failures are recorded and the job exits 101
unless a halt or wave gate applies. Configuration loading exits 2 for every
cause (3 for `config_lock_violation`), whatever the code's own exit, because the
configuration stage has one exit contract. `—` means the code does not set the exit by
itself. **Unclassified** codes are fallbacks used only when no specific cause is
known.

## Record reasons

Codes recorded for commands that were not started or were stopped.

| Code | Category | Exit | Retryable | Cause |
|---|---|---:|:---:|---|
| `cancelled` | shutdown | 113 | no | The activity was cancelled before the command finished or started. |
| `device_errors` | device | — | no | Scoreboard summary code when one or more devices in the activity failed; per-device records carry the specific codes. |
| `halt_error_count` | halt | 102 | no | A run-wide halt on the failure count stopped the command from starting. |
| `halt_error_percent` | halt | 103 | no | A run-wide halt on the failure percentage stopped the command from starting. |
| `halt_host_key_mismatch` | halt | 114 | no | A run-wide halt on a changed host key stopped the command from starting. |
| `halt_invalid_dispatch_mode` | internal | — | no | The dispatcher rejected an unknown dispatch mode, so no command started. |
| `run_halted` | halt | — | no | The run halted for a reason with no more specific code. |
| `shutdown_forced` | shutdown | 106 | no | The daemon was stopped with `--force` while the job was running; its unfinished units are `incomplete_shutdown`. |
| `shutdown_grace_expired` | shutdown | 106 | no | The daemon's shutdown grace expired while the job was running; its unfinished units are `incomplete_shutdown`. |
| `wave_gate_error_count` | halt | 104 | no | An adaptive-wave gate on the failure count stopped the command from starting. |
| `wave_gate_error_percent` | halt | 105 | no | An adaptive-wave gate on the failure percentage stopped the command from starting. |

## Notices

Warnings that do not fail the activity.

| Code | Category | Exit | Retryable | Cause |
|---|---|---:|:---:|---|
| `capacity_assessment` | notice | — | no | An exercise read the capacity ledgers without taking a lease: the server limit and its live entries, and each target's device cap and live entries. |
| `cloginrc_directive_ignored` | notice | — | no | The `.cloginrc` file uses a directive karvi reads but ignores. |
| `collection_write_failed` | notice | — | no | A device's collection file could not be written or renamed into place (the temporary in the collection directory, the disk, the rename): the device's previous file is kept, the job continues, and the warning names the device. A warning, not a failure of the job. |
| `crun_after_failed` | notice | — | no | The `crun.after` hook could not be started, exited non-zero, or ran past `crun.after-timeout` and was ended; the message names the path and the cause. The collection stands as written and the run's exit code is unchanged; the audit holds a `crun.after.failed` event. |
| `daemon_absent` | notice | — | no | A dry-run found no daemon answering at the socket; a live run would launch one. |
| `daemon_environment_secret_variable` | notice | — | no | A daemon started outside the launcher inherited `NETUSER`, `NETPASS`, or `NETENABLE`; the daemon does not read them, and the notice names the variable only. |
| `dispatch_assessment` | notice | — | no | An exercise reports the effective dispatch mode, width, and wave settings. |
| `follow_output_omitted` | notice | — | no | A followed record's output is left out of the follow stream: its `commands.jsonl` line is more than `daemon.max-ipc-frame-bytes` allows in a frame, or it passed `output.spool-threshold-bytes` in a job that keeps no `commands.jsonl`. The daemon sends the record with `output` empty and this notice in its place, `output_bytes` and `output_sha256` intact; the text renderer prints the message where the output would stand and `jsonl` carries the record as sent. The message names the size and where the output is: `commands.jsonl` when the job keeps it, or not kept. The key goes up to 64 MiB. |
| `host_key_enrollment` | notice | — | no | An exercise reports whether the target's host key is enrolled in the daemon's trust store under a policy that does not require it. |
| `icmp_assessment` | notice | — | no | An exercise detected the ICMP gate's method (ping socket or system ping) without sending a probe. |
| `icmp_packet_loss` | notice | — | no | The ICMP gate received one validated reply of two; the device proceeds and its first record carries the notice. |
| `output_text_write_failed` | notice | — | no | A device's `output.TARGET.txt` cannot be created or appended to. The job continues: the device's records are in `commands.jsonl`, its text file is left as it is from then on, and the text can be derived from the records. |
| `platform_not_set` | notice | — | no | An inventory row has no platform and its source no `defaults.platform`: the device proceeds as `platform-resolution.default` when configured, else `generic`, the client prints a warning line at planning, and the device's first record carries the notice with `supplied` (empty), `source`, and `used`; a direct target without `--platform` takes no notice. |
| `platform_unknown_fallback` | notice | — | no | An inventory row named a platform that is not known and `platform-resolution.on-unknown` is `warn`: the device proceeds as `platform-resolution.unknown-fallback`, the client prints a warning line at planning, and the device's first record carries the notice with `supplied`, `source`, and `used`. |
| `prompt_not_observed_after_blind_send` | notice | — | no | The prompt did not return after a blind command (`--blind`, `--blind-return N`, or a trailing `\r`), within `execution.blind-wait` or before the session ended; the record is a success holding all bytes read, with `blind_returns`, `blind_wait`, and `reason` (`blind_wait_expired` or `session_ended`), and the session is closed. |
| `resolution_notice` | notice | — | no | Name resolution reports a non-fatal notice for the target; a planning warning on stderr, not a record field. |
| `session_init_command_failed` | notice | — | no | A session-init profile command failed under `on-error = "continue"` with the session usable; the rest was sent and the device's first requested record carries the notice, with the profile, `command_index`, and code. |
| `spool_width_narrowed` | notice | — | no | `freecheck` is `auto` and the volume holding `spooldir` has less free space than the job's worst case, its width × `output.max-command-bytes` above the other places' estimates and the floor, but at least one limit: the job runs at the width that fits and the warning names the volume's paths, the free bytes, the limit, the fixed bytes, and the width chosen, on the client's standard error in process and on the receipt and the follow start under the daemon. Below one limit the job is refused with `output_preflight_space`. |
| `transport_assessment` | notice | — | no | An exercise located the target's transport implementation and, for the system kind, the askpass helper, without opening a session. |
